title: The Blog Bot Finally Checks Before It Publishes | vitalii.no
description:
Dictating a post to the Telegram /blog bot used to publish it immediately, with the model guessing at context it didn't actually have. It would invent details about my projects, or miss ones I'd mentioned on a different day, and there was no step to catch a bad draft before it was already live on the site.

I built a shared author-brain loader that reads three sources in parallel before any post gets written: my own filtered personal notes, a list of every project I've built, and a journal of dated one-line entries I append myself, by Telegram command or over SSH. Both entry points check everything against a list of secret patterns — API keys, tokens, private keys — and refuse to save anything that matches. The writer now asks a clarifying question instead of inventing when something's missing, and saves the result unpublished until I review it with Publish, Edit, Regenerate or Cancel buttons.

Publish is now the only action that makes a post go live, and for the first time all three /blog entry points — typed text, dictated voice, and a waiting-text flow — route through the exact same draft-then-publish check.
